questions.stem: Statements: 'All roses are flowers. Some flowers fade quickly.' Conclusion: 'Some roses fade quickly.' Does the conclusion follow?
questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Some flowers fade quickly' — these could be non-rose flowers. We cannot distribute the 'some' flowers that fade specifically onto roses. The conclusion does not necessarily follow.

questions.stem: Statements: 'Some cats are dogs. All dogs are animals.' Conclusions: I. Some cats are animals. II. Some animals are cats. Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Some cats are dogs + All dogs are animals → Some cats are animals (I follows). From 'Some cats are animals', by conversion: Some animals are cats (II follows). Both follow.

questions.stem: Argument: 'Should smoking be banned in public places? YES — because passive smoking is harmful to non-smokers.' Is this argument strong or weak?
questions.explanation: A is correct. The argument directly addresses harm caused to non-smokers — a third party. Protecting others from harm is a strong and relevant reason to support a public ban.

questions.stem: Statements: 'All managers are leaders. No leaders are lazy. Some lazy people are students.' Conclusions: I. No managers are lazy. II. Some students are not leaders. Which follow?
questions.explanation: C is correct. All managers=leaders + No leaders=lazy → No managers=lazy (I follows). No leaders=lazy → No lazy=leaders (conversion). Some lazy=students → these students are not leaders (II follows). Both follow.

questions.stem: Statement: 'The company's profits dropped 20% last year despite increased advertising spending.' Conclusion: 'Increased advertising does not guarantee increased profits.' Does the conclusion follow?
questions.explanation: A is correct. The statement is direct evidence that advertising spending increased yet profits fell. This validates the conclusion that advertising alone does not guarantee profits.

questions.stem: Statements: 'No scientists are poets. All poets are artists.' Conclusions: I. No scientists are artists. II. Some artists are not scientists. Which follow?
questions.explanation: B is correct. All poets=artists → some artists are poets. No scientists=poets → those poet-artists are not scientists → Some artists are not scientists (II follows). I does not follow: scientists could still be non-poet artists; we can't conclude 'no scientists are artists'.

questions.stem: Argument: 'Should private schools be abolished? No — because private schools provide better quality education.' Is this argument strong?
questions.explanation: A is correct. The argument directly addresses the core issue (education quality) and provides a substantive reason against abolition. It is strong because quality of education is central to the purpose of schools.

questions.stem: Statements: 'All fruits have seeds. Mangoes are fruits.' Conclusions: I. Mangoes have seeds. II. All seeds come from fruits. Which follow?
questions.explanation: A is correct. All fruits have seeds + Mangoes are fruits → Mangoes have seeds (I follows). II says 'All seeds come from fruits' — the premise only says fruits have seeds, not that only fruits have seeds. II does not follow.

questions.stem: Statements: 'Most employees who work overtime are stressed. Rajan works overtime regularly. Stressed employees often have health issues.' Conclusion: 'Rajan likely has health issues.' Does the conclusion follow?

options.option_text: Conclusion follows as a probable inference

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Most' and 'often' introduce probability, not certainty. Rajan is likely stressed (most overtime workers are) and likely has health issues (stressed employees often do). The conclusion is appropriately qualified ('likely') — it follows as a probable inference, not a definite one.

questions.stem: Statements: 'All banks charge interest.' 'Cooperative societies do not charge interest.' 'Moneylenders charge high interest.' Conclusions: I. Cooperative societies are not banks. II. Moneylenders are banks. Which follow?
questions.explanation: A is correct. All banks charge interest; cooperatives do not → cooperatives cannot be banks (I follows). Moneylenders charge interest, but not all interest-chargers are banks; the statement does not establish moneylenders as banks (II does not follow).
